sources.note: Primary-source pointer only: the site is a JS-driven page and advisory text could not be machine-verified at build time.

facts.quote: remaining below the pre-war level of 75 ships per day
facts.text: Bab-el-Mandeb traffic was ~31 ships/day as of May 2026 vs a pre-war 75/day.

facts.quote: they announced a blockade of Saudi Arabian ports and ships in the Bab-el-Mandeb
facts.text: Houthis resumed attacks on Saudi Arabia on 13 July 2026 and by 20 July announced a blockade of Saudi ports and ships in the Bab-el-Mandeb.

facts.quote: ten days of travel, and US$1,000,000 in fuel costs to each voyage
facts.text: Routing around the Cape of Good Hope adds ~11,000 nm, ten days of travel and ~US$1M in fuel per voyage (vessel-level, not per box).

facts.quote: Some major shipping corporations, such as Maersk, have since resumed their Red Sea routes, while others have held off
facts.text: After the Oct 2025 Gaza ceasefire some carriers (e.g. Maersk) resumed Red Sea routings; others held off.
The Suez route shortens Arabian Sea to London by about 8,900 km: ~10 days at 20 knots.

facts.quote: has been largely blocked by Iran since 28 February 2026
facts.text: Hormuz shipping has been largely blocked by Iran since 28 Feb 2026.

facts.quote: Major container shipping companies, including Maersk, CMA CGM, and Hapag-Lloyd, suspended transits through the strait
facts.text: Maersk, CMA CGM and Hapag-Lloyd suspended transits through the strait (and related routes such as the Red Sea).

facts.quote: a fall of 90.1% year on year
facts.text: Jebel Ali handled 374,000 TEU in Q2 2026, down 90.1% year on year.

facts.quote: Tracked transits through the strait fell from about 90 a day before the war to a handful
facts.text: Tracked Hormuz transits fell from ~90/day pre-war to a handful.

facts.quote: began building two terminals at Fujairah, outside the strait
facts.text: DP World began building two terminals at Fujairah, outside the strait; cargo has been rerouted overland.

facts.quote: From 15 September 2026, the number of ships allowed to pass through it dropped to 32
facts.text: Panama Canal daily transit slots cut from 36 to 34 (3 Sep 2026) and 32 (15 Sep 2026) on low rainfall amid El Niño.

facts.quote: paid a record US$5.3 million in an auction for priority passage
facts.text: Aug 2026: record US$5.3M paid at auction for priority passage of one LPG tanker, amid restrictions tied to drought.

facts.quote: In normal times, 36 ships can transit the canal each day
facts.text: Normal capacity is 36 transits/day; 22/day in Dec 2023 drought.
